key_insight: Fun-DDPS couples a function-space diffusion prior over geological fields with a differentiable neural-operator surrogate to decouple forward physics from prior learning, enabling fast, gradient-based posterior sampling for both forward and inverse CCS tasks.
problem_solved: Addresses the ill-posed, computationally expensive inverse problem in Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS): recovering high-dimensional subsurface geological parameters from sparse observations while quantifying uncertainty efficiently.
method: Train a single-channel function-space diffusion model to learn a realistic prior distribution over geomodels (geological parameter fields).
Train a differentiable neural operator surrogate to approximate the expensive PDE-based forward simulator (flow/transport) for fast predictions and gradients.
Combine the diffusion prior with the neural operator to perform conditioned sampling/inference (posterior estimation) for inverse problems and to accelerate forward uncertainty propagation.
impact: Provides a scalable, differentiable framework for fast forward simulations and principled posterior inference under sparse data—useful for practitioners needing uncertainty-aware, physics-informed generative models and rapid inverse solutions in geoscience and other physical domains.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: diffusion prior module + neural operator surrogate + conditioning loop for inverse sampling
Before/after map: example geomodel samples with uncertainty bands versus recovered posterior samples given sparse observations
Performance chart: speed and accuracy comparison against traditional PDE solvers and non-differentiable priors
Flow diagram contrasting forward prediction (geomodel → observables) and inverse inference (observations → posterior geomodels)
paper_title: Function-Space Decoupled Diffusion for Forward and Inverse Modeling in Carbon Capture and Storage
paper_authors: Xin Ju, Jiachen Yao, Anima Anandkumar, Sally M. Benson, Gege Wen
